items.headline: Micron's AI-memory quarter quadruples revenue and reports HBM sold out through 2026
items.diff_narrative: A fresh memory-supply thread with no prior-day antecedent. Yesterday's slate ran on edge models (Liquid AI LFM2.5-230M), Qualcomm's Modular acquisition, Unsloth fine-tuning and OWASP's prompt-injection reframe; none touched the memory layer. Today opens it with Micron's June 25 fiscal-Q3-2026 print: $41.46B revenue up ~346% year-over-year, fifth straight record quarter, Q4 guided to ~$50B, and a structural HBM signal that CEO Sanjay Mehrotra can fill only half to two-thirds of demand, with all of 2026 supply sold out under multi-year deals, HBM4 past $1B and ramping ~2x faster than HBM3E, plus 16 take-or-pay agreements locking in roughly $100B of minimum revenue and $22B of upfront cash. The new read-through is that AI compute is now memory-gated, not just GPU-gated.

items.headline: Qualcomm names Meta as first data-center CPU customer and lays out the Dragonfly accelerator roadmap
items.diff_narrative: This advances yesterday's Qualcomm story to a new state. On June 28 the thread was the ~$3.92B Modular acquisition plus reported Tenstorrent talks, framed as assembling a silicon-agnostic compiler layer against Nvidia's CUDA lock-in. Today the same June 24 Investor Day surfaces its hardware half: a full Dragonfly data-center roadmap that for the first time attaches a named hyperscaler, with Meta committing to the Dragonfly C1000 CPU (claimed >2x perf-per-watt) for its next-gen server fleet at 2028 availability, alongside the Dragonfly AI300 inference accelerator (claimed 4x-8x perf-per-watt, sampling 2028) and a High Bandwidth Compute memory tier (up to 54x bandwidth over AI200). The shift is from the compiler/M&A angle to a concrete CPU-plus-accelerator-plus-named-customer inference-economics attack on Nvidia, with the standing caveat that first commercial sampling is still two years out.

items.headline: Gartner puts agent software at $206.5B for 2026 as a $1.5B Indian sovereign-AI unicorn shows where spend pools
items.diff_narrative: A new corporate-spend and sovereign-AI thread with no equivalent yesterday, which stayed on models, tooling and security rather than enterprise demand. Today pairs the demand and supply sides: Gartner now pegs AI-agent software spending at about $206.5B in 2026, up ~139% from $86.4B in 2025 and on track for $376.3B in 2027 — nearly triple the 47% growth of overall AI spend — with a standing caution that over 40% of agentic-AI projects may be cancelled by end-2027. On the supply side, HCLTech led a $234M first close of Sarvam's $300M Series B at a $1.5B valuation (a ~10.5% stake from its own $150M check), minting India's newest AI unicorn around an in-country frontier model for coding, agentic and cybersecurity work. The new framing is that the agent-spend wave is now pulling national-champion model builders into the capital flow, not just US frontier labs.

items.headline: AI events to plan around now: World's Fair main program opens today
items.diff_narrative: The events tracker continues across all three sub-tracks and advances its calendar by one state-change: the AI Engineer World's Fair main program (June 29 - July 2, Moscone West) is no longer 'opens this week' but opening today, anchored by the Coding Agents keynote and expo, with Autoresearch (July 1) and Harness Engineering (July 2) keynotes now named across ~12 parallel tracks each. Yesterday's framing of the passed weekend hackathon and Sunday orientation is dropped as date-passed. The standing AI-security dates (SecurityWeek AI Risk Summit Aug 11-12, Black Hat USA plus its AI Summit and DEF CON 34 in early August, OWASP Global AppSec USA Nov 5-6, Zenity's summit series) and AI-chip dates (AMD Advancing AI July 22-23, Hot Chips Aug 23-25, AI Infra Summit Sept 15-17) carry forward unchanged, with GitHub Universe (Oct 28-29) and AWS re:Invent (Nov 30 - Dec 4) still held further out.
